root.claim: A multitape Turing machine multiplies $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: chain reductions from the integer product to a convolution over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$, compute it with accelerated synthetic transforms, then recover the exact product

motivation.text: Each stage changes the problem into one whose transform uses only shifts, address rearrangements and butterflies, which the two fast tape procedures speed up; precision analysis then gives exactness.

root.salient: The logarithmic factor has the strict power (lg n)^{1-kappa} with a tiny fixed kappa, below the conjectured n log n.
